slides.heading: Reception — Autumn 1, Week 2
slides.sub: New sounds taught directly, practised and applied in words, captions and the matching decodable book.

slides.heading: Mon
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "s" (/s/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="sun" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="sun"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Sula the snail slides along so slowly, leaving a soft 'sss' trail behind her wherever she goes.

character.name: Sula
character.blurb: Sula is a gentle garden snail who never rushes, always leaving a shining trail as she hisses her way along the path.

slides.pronunciation_note: A long hiss you can hold for as long as you like — 'sssss', not 'suh'. Don't let a vowel sneak onto the end.
slides.formation_cue: Start at the top right. Curve up and round to the left, then across and back round to the right, and round to the left at the bottom. Finish at the bottom left.
slides.formation_rhyme: Curve back, then curve round again.
slides.action: Trace a slow wavy line in the air with one finger while whispering a long 'sssss', following the shape of Sula's trail.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="sun" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="sun"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.note: Not enough sounds taught yet to build a whole word — practise oral blending and sound recognition only today.

slides.heading: Tue
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "a" (/æ/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="apple" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="apple"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Acer the acorn drops from the branch and bounces on the ground three times — 'a, a, a'!

character.name: Acer
character.blurb: Acer is a small round acorn with a fuzzy little cap who loves to bounce down from the tallest branch.

slides.pronunciation_note: A short, flat sound made with the mouth open wide — 'a' as in 'cat', not the long letter name.
slides.formation_cue: Start at the top right of a small round shape. Curve round to the left and all the way back up to where you started, then go straight down without lifting. Finish on the line.
slides.formation_rhyme: Round and over, down we go.
slides.action: Crouch down and spring up a tiny bit three times, like Acer bouncing on the ground, saying 'a, a, a'.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="apple" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="apple"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.heading: Wed
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "t" (/t/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="tin" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="tin"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Tolly the feather taps gently on the twig every time the wind blows — 't, t, t'.

character.name: Tolly
character.blurb: Tolly is a light little feather who loves to rest on twigs and tap out a soft beat when the breeze catches him.

slides.pronunciation_note: A quick, light tap of the tongue behind the top teeth — 't', not 'tuh'.
slides.formation_cue: Start a little above the small letters. Pull straight down and finish on the line with a small curve to the right. Lift, then draw a short line across at the top of the small letters, from left to right.
slides.formation_rhyme: Tall line down, cross near the top.
slides.action: Tap one fingertip lightly on the back of your other hand twice, like Tolly tapping the twig, saying 't, t'.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="tin" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="tin"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.heading: Thu
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "p" (/p/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="pig" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="pig"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Poppy the pinecone pops open one scale at a time in the warm sun — 'p, p, p'.

character.name: Poppy
character.blurb: Poppy is a tightly closed pinecone who loves warm, sunny days because that's when her scales pop open one by one.

slides.pronunciation_note: A little puff of air as closed lips pop open — 'p', not 'puh'.
slides.formation_cue: Start at the top of the small letters. Pull straight down below the line, go back up the same line, then curve round to the right and back. Finish where the curve meets the line.
slides.formation_rhyme: Down below, loop round the top.
slides.action: Press your lips together and let them pop open softly with a little puff of air, like one of Poppy's scales popping, saying 'p, p'.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="pig" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="pig"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.heading: Fri
slides.objective: Revisit everything taught this week, read the matched decodable book, and check how securely it has been learned.
